hints: Remember you need to check two separate conditions here, one for the C=C double bond and one for a chiral carbon.
Look first at the left-hand C=C in each structure and cross out any where one carbon has two identical groups, as cis-trans is then impossible.
For the survivors, check the single-bonded carbon for four different groups attached, which would give a chiral centre and optical isomerism.
walkthrough:
**Recall the two conditions**

Great start, let us get the rules clear in our minds. Cis-trans needs a C=C where each C has two different groups.

Optical needs a chiral carbon with four different groups: $$ \text{chiral C = C with 4 different substituents} $$

**Test for cis-trans isomerism**

Look at the C=C from left to right. In A the left C has $\text{Br}$ and $\text{Br}$, identical, so no cis-trans. In D the left C also has $\text{Br}$ and $\text{Br}$, so no cis-trans.

In B the left C has $\text{Br}$ and $\text{I}$, and the right C has $\text{H}$ and a carbon group, both different, so cis-trans is possible. In C the left C has $\text{Br}$ and $\text{Cl}$, and the right C has $\text{H}$ and a carbon group, so cis-trans is also possible.

**Test for optical isomerism**

Now check the saturated carbon for four different groups. In B the carbon is $\text{C(Cl)(H)(Br)(C=C)}$, all four are different, so it is chiral and shows optical isomerism.

In C the similar carbon is $\text{C(Br)(Br)(Cl)(C=O)}$, with two $\text{Br}$ atoms identical, so it is achiral and shows no optical isomerism. Only B passes both tests.

options.A: Shows optical isomerism because the $\text{CHBrCl}$ carbon has four different groups, but no cis-trans isomerism because the left C of the C=C has two identical $\text{Br}$ atoms.
options.B: Shows both. The C=C has $\text{Br}$ vs $\text{I}$ on one end and $\text{H}$ vs carbon chain on the other, so cis-trans is possible. The $\text{CHBrCl}$ carbon is attached to $\text{Cl}$, $\text{H}$, $\text{Br}$ and the alkenyl group, so it is chiral and shows optical isomerism.
options.C: Shows cis-trans isomerism because the C=C has $\text{Br}$ vs $\text{Cl}$ and $\text{H}$ vs acyl group, but no optical isomerism because the $\text{CBr}_{2}\text{Cl}$ carbon has two identical $\text{Br}$ atoms and is not chiral.
options.D: Shows optical isomerism because the $\text{CHClI}$ carbon has four different groups, but no cis-trans isomerism because the left C of the C=C has two identical $\text{Br}$ atoms.
